hook: A trained detector finds heart structures in echo images where general AI models find 3% or fewer
hook_turn: where general AI models find 3% or fewer
summary: General and medical vision-language models almost never located cardiac structures in echocardiograms. EchoLens, a detector trained on expert-annotated structures and Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% of structures and matched a blinded expert on placement. Training data came from a small patient group, and external checks relied on two physicians judging detections.
title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
